extracted.intended_audience: DoD managers, contracting officers, and analysts conducting or overseeing A-76 competitive sourcing studies and Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF) activities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for conducting A-76 competitive sourcing studies in the context of Defense Working Capital Fund activities, including cost comparison, source selection, appeals, transition, activity-based costing, and suitability of A-76 for already-competitive WCF organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source selection: best value selection
rubrics_metrics.description: From the proposals and any changes made, the CO selects a single firm based on their ability to meet the requirements of the MEO. The selection is a 'best value' choice vice the 'cost comparisons' method used later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussions (written or oral) with bidders aim to resolve discrepancies in cost proposals and must be in accordance with the FAR. The expected outcome bases the choice of contractor on the greatest overall value to the Government in response to the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison (SSA determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Source Selection Authority (SSA) compares the in-house MEO and IHCE with the selected private sector proposal to determine that the Government technical proposal will provide the same level of support and performance as the selected bid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Government in-house proposal is deficient, revise it to ensure a fair comparison. The objective is to ensure the two proposals provide the same scope of work and level of performance and to base the final selection on lowest cost; the cost comparison creates a tentative decision to accept either the in-house MEO or the contractor bid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum cost differential requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a minimum cost differential requirement: the contractor proposal must be 10% lower than the Government proposal or $10M less over the performance period, whichever is less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the contractor proposal is above the threshold, the function remains in the government. The differential accounts for conversion costs to a private contractor when savings are small. Upon passing the threshold test, the Contracting Officer informs the Unit Commander of the tentative decision to prepare for the official announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative appeals: standing and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals to the A-76 steps must be in writing and received by the contracting officer within the review period. The contractor submitting the appeal must have submitted a proposal for bid; Federal employees or government agencies eligible for replacement by outsourcing may also submit an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appeals process focuses on errors made in the cost comparison steps; overall, the cost comparison is the most frequent point or issue of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition Plan (TP) content and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Administrative Appeal process is completed the final selectee (government MEO or contractor) begins the Transition Plan (TP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TP must address personnel management issues, transfer of equipment and inventories, and any procedural changes. Implementation follows immediately upon selection and precedes the Post-MEO Performance Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-MEO Performance Review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: If the organization implements the MEO, conduct a formal review and inspection following the end of the first full year of performance (Post-MEO Performance Review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review confirms the MEO was implemented in accordance with the Transition Plan, establishes the MEO's ability to perform the services of the PWS, and confirms that actual costs are within the estimates contained in the in-house estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post A-76 actions: QASP implementation and periodic review
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of the A-76, the new organization begins full performance and the Government implements the QASP regardless of the final choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization must review the QASP periodically to ensure the validity of the PWS set by the A-76. If the organization implements the Government MEO, a formal review and inspection at the end of the first year verifies that the MEO is in accordance with the Government Management plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification criteria for Working Capital Operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Three required elements for an organization to qualify as a Working Capital Operation: (1) an identifiable product or service; (2) customers that will buy the product or service; (3) a cost accounting system to provide total cost visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three elements are mandatory to qualify as a WCF operation and underpin the DWCF financial structure's customer-provider relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between Supply Management and non-Supply Management WCFs
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply Management (Stock Fund) operations receive contract authority permitting obligations in advance of customer orders, while non-Supply Management (Industrial) areas must have immediate budgetary resources in the form of customer orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although actual outlay for non-supply may occur later, the resources still must be available; this difference affects cash flow, obligation authority, and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: WCF business model: break-even total cost recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: A WCF organization finances operations with initial working capital and subsequently through customer orders; the primary goal is to manage total cost of delivery and recover all costs on a break-even basis over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund must maintain enough revenue to cover all expenses or cease to exist; replenishment occurs when the organization invoices and receives payment from customers. The cash balance should operate to maintain a positive balance and strive for accumulated operating result (AOR) of zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity-Based Costing (ABC) and unit cost definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Unit cost is defined as costs divided by the measurement of output (cost driver). WCF managers use Activity-Based Costing to capture and allocate costs across a specific product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of cost drivers include Direct Labor Hours or Units of Goods Sold. In the ABC model, the providing activity influences the numerator (costs) and the customer influences the denominator (output). Understanding drivers allows managers to determine unit cost and make informed decisions on labor and material to produce competitive rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost element definitions and allocation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost elements for WCF include: Direct Costs (directly attributable to product/output), Indirect Costs (not directly tied to operational output, allocated over outputs), General & Administration (G&A) costs (not contributing to specific product, allocated across outputs), Variable costs (vary with workload), and Fixed costs (remain the same during operations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct costs should be allocated over individual output units; indirect and G&A are overhead and allocated across outputs. Distinguishing cost types informs unit cost calculations and rate-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: NAVSISA rate-setting equation and billable-hours model
rubrics_metrics.description: NAVSISA determines Annual Stabilized Rate using Billable Hours/Billable Work Years: Rate = (All Labor + Non-labor - (Profit + Loss)) / (Billable Employees x Billable Hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time distribution reduces available hours to Billable Hours (example yields 1650). The numerator includes all employee costs, overhead, and prior-year gains/losses; only billable employees/hours determine revenue, which means revenue-generating functions carry costs of non-revenue functions. This incentivizes minimizing labor costs, maximizing billable hours sold, and reducing overhead to maintain competitive market rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: DWCF goals/advantages as evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Desired DWCF attributes include: identifying total/'true' cost of goods and services; underlining cost consequences of choices; providing managers financial authority and flexibility; improving cost estimates and control; placing customers in position to evaluate price and quality; allowing flexibility/security due to no fiscal year limitations; establishing stabilized unit prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These advantages serve as performance and design criteria when evaluating WCF implementations and whether a WCF is functioning as intended in promoting efficient, market-like decision making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of applying A-76 to WCF activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 is a lengthy (18–36 month) process designed to introduce competition to create economy and productivity, but it may be inappropriate for WCF activities that already operate in a competitive marketplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the WCF already uses market mechanisms (packaging products, PWS/QASP-like cost-driver evaluation, continuous cost comparisons) the A-76 may offer only a marginal 'second opinion' at significant time and labor cost; A-76's single-point-in-time analysis contrasts with the dynamic requirements of market-driven WCFs.
